sessions.phase_label: Final Word-template corrections and PowerPoint scoping

requirements.title: Consistent Style-System Deployment
requirements.definition: The prescribed Word style catalog must be implemented consistently in every applicable template.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the availability and consistent deployment of the style catalog; typography, naming, list behavior, bullets, and theme colors remain independently changeable Requirements.

requirements.title: PBU-Prefixed Style Names
requirements.definition: Applicable active Word styles must use the requested PBU-prefixed naming convention when required for the finalized style system.
requirements.boundary_note: Style naming can change independently of style formatting or availability; the brief expresses some conditionality, so the final naming obligation requires lifecycle review.

requirements.title: Named-Style Typography
requirements.definition: Named text styles must apply the confirmed font sizes, weights, fonts, italics, and related typography specifications.
requirements.boundary_note: Individual specifications such as Title size, Heading 3 weight, and caption typography are attributes of the shared typography mechanism rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Tab-Based List Hierarchy
requirements.definition: Relevant list styles must let users create and navigate consistently aligned sub-levels using the Tab key.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers hierarchy and Tab indentation behavior; bullet appearance and numbered-list alignment have separate failure and correction trajectories.

requirements.title: Bullet Visual Design
requirements.definition: Bullet glyphs at each level must use the requested design, scale proportionately with text, and remain visually and vertically aligned.
requirements.boundary_note: Includes level-specific bullet glyph and size attributes, including the green fourth-level bullet; it excludes Tab hierarchy and numbered-list behavior.

requirements.title: Numbered-List Formatting
requirements.definition: Numbered lists must retain correct numbering, style assignment, indentation, and alignment as item numbers grow.
requirements.boundary_note: Separates numbered-list alignment and numbering behavior from graphic bullet styling and general Tab-based hierarchy.

requirements.title: Controlled Theme Color Palette
requirements.definition: Templates must expose the intended customer theme colors without unrelated color options.
requirements.boundary_note: Color-palette configuration can be changed independently of typography and bullet design.

requirements.title: Danish Word Language Configuration
requirements.definition: The Word templates must use the client-confirmed Danish language configuration as their intended default.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers document language configuration rather than the visible wording of style names, labels, or placeholders.

requirements.title: Danish Template Interface Text
requirements.definition: User-facing style names, field labels, and placeholder instructions must use the confirmed Danish wording.
requirements.boundary_note: Visible Danish copy is independent of Word's underlying proofing/default-language configuration and of the behavioral rules for the fields.

requirements.title: Legacy Copy-Paste Stability
requirements.definition: Content moved from legacy PBU templates into the new templates must preserve a predictable and usable layout and style result.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the end-to-end legacy-content transfer behavior; pasted-table containment and post-paste manual line breaks are independently testable sub-behaviors.

requirements.title: Pasted Table and Column Integrity
requirements.definition: Pasted table layouts and columns must remain stable and contained within the intended page margins.
requirements.boundary_note: Targets the specific table and column containment path rather than all copy-paste behavior or Master-template reusable-table behavior.

requirements.title: Post-Paste Manual Line Breaks
requirements.definition: Users must be able to create reliable manual line breaks after inserting content from legacy documents.
requirements.boundary_note: This requirement is limited to line breaks following pasted content; normal Enter behavior inside interactive fields has a separate lifecycle.

requirements.title: Cross-User Rendering Consistency
requirements.definition: The templates should render and behave consistently for different users of current Microsoft Word for Windows.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers environment-level consistency across users rather than any one bullet, field, or layout defect.

requirements.title: Master-Template Table Interaction Stability
requirements.definition: Reusable table elements in the Master template must remain usable and structurally stable during normal customer editing.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers normal use of Master-template table elements; duplicated field content and containment of externally pasted tables are separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Robust Text-Entry Field Architecture
requirements.definition: Ordinary text-entry areas must use a robust editable representation appropriate for users, avoiding unsuitable legacy developer fields where they add no value.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns the choice of field representation; clear-on-click, labels, field visibility, specialized controls, and multiline behavior remain independently testable.

requirements.title: Clear Placeholder on Activation
requirements.definition: Activating an applicable insert field must let the user replace its placeholder directly without manually selecting and deleting the existing text.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers replacement interaction only; persistent help labels and visual field discoverability are separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Persistent Interactive-Field Help Labels
requirements.definition: Each applicable control field must have a help label matching its intended placeholder so users can recover the field's purpose after replacing its content.
requirements.boundary_note: Label wording and persistence form one help mechanism; Danish localization of that wording is owned by the localization Requirement.

requirements.title: Interactive-Field Visual Discoverability
requirements.definition: Editable fields must remain visibly identifiable to users, including when their editable content is empty.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers visual indication of editable areas, not the underlying field technology or the separate hover-label behavior.

requirements.title: Independent Field Content
requirements.definition: Interactive fields must be unique instances so editing one field does not duplicate or synchronize unintended content elsewhere.
requirements.boundary_note: Content duplication is independently testable from table stability, placeholder clearing, and label behavior.

requirements.title: Interactive-Field Formatting Retention
requirements.definition: Entering or replacing content in an interactive field must preserve the intended field typography and formatting.
requirements.boundary_note: Formatting retention can fail independently of whether a field clears, wraps, or duplicates its content.

requirements.title: Dropdown and Checklist Controls
requirements.definition: The designated Board Meeting dropdown and Indstilling checklist interactions must remain implemented as specialized controls.
requirements.boundary_note: These specialized selection controls were explicitly retained even while ordinary text-entry controls were reconsidered.

requirements.title: Consistent Date-Picker Fields
requirements.definition: Applicable templates must provide the accepted selectable date-field behavior with the confirmed day/month/year presentation.
requirements.boundary_note: Date selection and formatting form one specialized field mechanism, separate from ordinary text placeholders.

requirements.title: Normal-Enter Multiline Field Entry
requirements.definition: Designated text-entry fields must accept normal Enter for multiple lines with usable paragraph spacing rather than requiring Shift+Enter.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers explicit Enter-key and paragraph-break behavior; automatic wrapping and horizontal containment are separate.

requirements.title: Text-Field Word Wrap and Column Containment
requirements.definition: Text entered in constrained template areas must wrap automatically without pushing neighboring columns outside their intended positions.
requirements.boundary_note: Automatic wrapping and horizontal containment can fail even when normal Enter is supported, so they remain separate from multiline entry.

requirements.title: Interactive-Field Cell Padding
requirements.definition: Text in the reviewed row and column fields must maintain sufficient spacing from surrounding borders and lines.
requirements.boundary_note: Cell padding is independently adjustable from paragraph-break support, page-fit spacing, and fixed outer margins.

requirements.title: Page Numbers Starting on Page Two
requirements.definition: The first page must omit its footer page number, with page numbering displayed from page two onward.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a discrete footer behavior and does not include general page spacing or margins.

requirements.title: Compact Template Page-Fit Spacing
requirements.definition: Template spacing must be compact enough for the intended content to fit within the required page layout without losing readability.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers overall page-fit spacing rather than local field-cell padding or hard-return behavior.

requirements.title: Fixed Content Margins
requirements.definition: Constrained content regions must retain fixed margins so entered text does not collapse the layout or obscure adjacent graphic elements.
requirements.boundary_note: Fixed outer margins and icon containment are distinct from text wrapping within fields and from table-paste containment.

requirements.title: Board Meeting Field Alignment
requirements.definition: The Board Meeting template's Item and Title fields must align with Topic, Proposal, and Start Time.
requirements.boundary_note: Field alignment is independently correctable from the workflow for inserting additional agenda rows.

requirements.title: Board Meeting Row-Insertion Workflow
requirements.definition: Users must be able to add another Board Meeting agenda item using the accepted insert-row and field-copy workflow without unintended border behavior.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns row creation and associated border behavior; automatic numbering and static field alignment are separate concerns.

requirements.title: Table Usage Guidance
requirements.definition: Provide a practical explanation or walkthrough showing users how to use the template table mechanisms correctly.
requirements.boundary_note: The requested guidance artifact is independent of fixing the underlying table behavior; generic testing activity is not included.

requirements.title: Versioned Complete Template Package
requirements.definition: Deliver the complete current set of template files as one consistently versioned package using the client-specified filename version.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an executable-artifact packaging and naming obligation; schedules, payment, and ordinary hand-off messages are excluded.

requirements.title: PowerPoint Template Built from Customer Design
requirements.definition: Create a new editable PowerPoint template from scratch using the design and graphic assets supplied by the customer.
requirements.boundary_note: Only the confirmed template deliverable is retained; logo placement, image masks, bullet limits, and other design questions remain unresolved rather than being assumed as accepted sub-Requirements.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client requires Danish defaults, while the freelancer says the document default will be English with Danish style names; the short client response may not unambiguously resolve the underlying language configuration.
The PBU style-prefix instruction is expressed conditionally and the delivery list says 'maybe'; later evidence should determine whether it became a firm naming Requirement.
The accepted architecture for ordinary text-entry areas is not fully stable: the discussion considers modern controls and plain text, while later messages again refer to control fields.
The freelancer proposes protecting content-control fields from accidental deletion, but the client's 'no further comments' does not clearly establish acceptance.
The exact Master-template table failures and requested checkbox-resizing behavior depend on unavailable attachments and may require further splitting if distinct table mechanisms are shown.

PowerPoint details concerning backgrounds, logo placement, image masks, highlighted bullets, responsive text behavior, and slide-specific spacing are questions or risks rather than confirmed requirements in the supplied history.
